bidding.thirteenRoundsMakeEveryCardCount: Thirteen rounds. Make every card count.
bidding.theRedSideBidsWithHeartsAnd: The red side bids with hearts ♥ and has diamond ♦ rewards; the black side bids with spades ♠ and has club ♣ rewards. Each player has thirteen bidding cards, A through K, valued 1–13, used once each. Every round reveals one reward from each side. Both players bid privately; the higher bid claims the entire pool. Bidding cards do not score points themselves.
bidding.aTiedBidCarriesTheRewardsInto: A tied bid carries the rewards into the next round. A tie in round thirteen discards the remaining pool. The higher final total wins; equal totals draw.
bidding.duringTheFirstTwelveRoundsJokerDecisions: During the first twelve rounds, joker decisions alternate, giving each player six opportunities. Each player may use their joker once to double their suit’s current reward. The decision lasts ten seconds; timeout saves the joker. Round thirteen has no joker decision. Each bidding phase lasts twenty seconds; an unlocked player times out with their lowest remaining card.
bidding.queueForUpTo120SecondsAnd: Queue for up to 120 seconds and cancel at any time before matching. Entry terms are fixed once queued. Surrender immediately concedes the game. Fees are charged from the losing entry; the winner gets their original principal and a general-credit prize. Draws and system cancellations refund both players. Complete game records are kept for thirty days.

blackjack.oneRoundEvery30SecondsUpTo: One round every 30 seconds, up to nine seats
blackjack.every30Seconds5SecondsForSeating: Every 30 seconds: 5 seconds for seating, 20 for simultaneous decisions and 5 for results. An early finish extends the result display; the next round keeps its scheduled start. An empty table creates no game.
blackjack.joiningReservesYourStakeUsingGameCredits: Joining reserves your stake, using game credits first and general credits for the remainder. The first nine accepted requests take seats. Waiting players keep their place across rounds and may leave for an original-asset refund. Seated players may leave before dealing. After playing, join the tail again explicitly; there is no automatic re-entry.
blackjack.sixCompleteDecksAreShuffledAnewEach: Six complete decks are shuffled anew each round. Aces count as 1 or 11; face cards count as 10. The dealer stands on soft 17 and peeks for blackjack. An original ace plus a ten-value card is a natural blackjack and beats an ordinary 21. No insurance, surrender, five-card bonus or side bets.
blackjack.splitEqualValueCardsOnceIntoTwo: Split equal-value cards once into two hands. Doubling after a normal split is allowed; split aces receive one card each and stand. Doubling reserves an equal stake and draws exactly one card. A split 21 is an ordinary win. One action per seat is processed each second, in rotating seat order. Other players do not change your hand revision. Unfinished hands stand at the deadline.
blackjack.grossReturnsAreZeroForALoss: Gross returns are zero for a loss, the stake for a push, twice the stake for a win and 2.5 times the stake for a natural. Platform, welfare and Thursday fees are each deducted per hand; all net proceeds are general credits. Rates freeze when you queue. At the default 1% each, a stake of 1,000 returns 970 on a push, 1,940 on a win and 2,425 on a natural. Long-term expected returns are negative.
blackjack.disconnectionDoesNotPauseTheGameA: Disconnection does not pause the game. A restart cancels only the current unsettled table and refunds every original payment; waiting players keep their queue. Committed results stay final. Personal history is available for 30 days, followed by anonymous game facts.

blackjack.onePlayerIsEnoughNineSeatsMaximum: One player is enough; nine seats maximum. Others watch and keep their queue position.
blackjack.everyStakeWasRefundedInItsOriginal: Every stake was refunded in its original assets without fees. Unseated waiters keep their position.
blackjack.yourPlaceRemainsValidAcrossRoundsYou: Your place remains valid across rounds. You may be seated next round automatically; leave at any time.

rules.title: How three-player RPS works
rules.goalBody: Each match has three randomly matched players. Everyone chooses rock, scissors, or paper: rock beats scissors, scissors beats paper, and paper beats rock.
rules.roundBody: All three choices stay hidden until the reveal, and a submitted choice cannot be changed. A gesture has a 20-second limit. The dealer then has 15 seconds to raise or decline, and both followers share a 15-second limit to call or surrender. On timeout, the game chooses a random gesture, treats the dealer as declining a raise, or treats a follower as surrendering.

score.same: If all three gestures are the same, or all three gestures are different, a Quick match splits the pot into thirds; Standard and Deathmatch carry the pot forward.
score.oneWinner: If one player beats two players who chose the same gesture, that player receives two-thirds of the pot and the other two receive one-sixth each.
score.twoWinners: If two players with the same gesture beat the third player, the two winners split the pot equally and the losing player receives nothing.

mode.quick: Quick: each player enters with the current base stake, there is one reveal, and the match ends.
mode.standard: Standard: each player enters with five times the current base stake. The dealer rotates for up to nine ordinary rounds. A tied pot must finish before the match can end. After a pot is settled, the match ends when nine ordinary rounds are complete or any player has less than one base stake left; every remaining in-game balance is then returned.
mode.deathmatch: Deathmatch: each player brings all positive available game and general credits, with at least the base stake, and cannot add credits from outside during the match. The first nine ordinary stakes use the base amount; it then rises to twice the base amount and rises by one more base amount after every three ordinary stakes. During a paid tied-pot continuation, the first three stakes use its starting amount and each later tie raises the next stake by one base amount. A settled pot ends the match if any player then has no credits left. When an ordinary stake leaves all three players at zero, that hand becomes the Ultimate Showdown.

rules.feesBody: Every entry, base stake, raise, or continuation stake is split using the rates shown on the page: platform, welfare pool, and Thursday pool. The remainder goes into the player pot, and the same stake is never split twice.
rules.dealerBody: Raises are available only in Standard and Deathmatch ordinary dealer rounds. After gestures are locked, the dealer may choose no raise or enter a positive whole-credit raise up to the smallest remaining whole-credit balance. If there is a raise, each of the other two players calls with the same amount or surrenders. No raise is a separate choice from entering 0.
rules.surrenderBody: If both followers surrender, the dealer takes the current pot. If one follower surrenders, that player gets nothing and the dealer and the other follower split the result: half each for the same gesture, or two-thirds and one-third when one beats the other.
rules.poolBody: In Standard and Deathmatch, a reveal with three equal scores and no surrender locks the pot instead of paying it out. There is no fixed limit on paid continuation rounds. Once no more credits are added, the players continue with free reveals; the third consecutive free tie starts the reminder, and the sixth consecutive free tie ends the match and sends the locked pot to the welfare pool.
rules.ultimateBody: The Ultimate Showdown has no dealer, raise, call, or surrender, and no new stake is added. A non-tie ends it with the normal sharing rules. A tie starts free reveals, with at most six free decisions; a sixth consecutive free tie ends the match and sends the locked pot to the welfare pool.
rules.queueBody: The three modes have separate queues. A queue can wait for up to 120 seconds; cancelling or timing out before a match refunds each wallet its original payment. Once a match starts, leaving the page or switching tabs does not pause the clock or cancel the match.
rules.statsBody: At the start of a match, each player sees the other two players’ combined lifetime RPS summary from before this match. Fewer than ten completed matches shows only the match count. The two public leaderboards cover the latest 30 days, are separate for each mode, and require at least ten completed matches in that mode.

privacy.fatFishBody: Fat Fish runs on your device. The original tab keeps a continuation capability in session storage and a bounded record of inputs and timing in IndexedDB so it can recover after a refresh. A copied tab cannot take over an active game. Local play records are cleared after a confirmed terminal result or expiry. The server receives the complete inputs for verification in bounded process memory and releases them after verification; it does not save complete inputs or per-tick replay in its database, logs or exports. Safe terminal summaries and seed commitments remain for 30 days. Unlocks, best scores and progress remain for the account lifetime. Account export includes only your safe summaries and progress, safe request-adaptation structure without configured values, and current eligibility; the two Fat Fish collections share a 10,000-row limit. Deleting your account removes personal progress and public ranking identity. Minimum same-identity reward claims and de-identified accounting facts may remain to prevent duplicate rewards and finish accounting. Administrator playtests do not charge, reward or rank. Lake Notes stores coins, experience, equipment, bait, fish, collections, contracts, the current cast, entry eligibility and exchange records on the server for use across devices and activity periods. Old local saves cannot become site assets. Completed records last 30 days and temporary operation receipts last 24 hours; the current or paused cast and profile follow the account lifetime. Input records are cleared after necessary verification. Your export includes the profile, cast, entry and exchange records, excluding unrevealed reward randomness. Deletion removes personal progress and links; settled accounting follows the existing anonymous retention policy. The browser may temporarily keep limited unconfirmed actions and connection progress, but connection drafts never store keys.
privacy.charityManagementBody: Administrators and current level-6 stewards can review donations and see the donor’s site ID, Discord ID, display name, recorded source details and donation/review notes. Level-5 trainees can see necessary information and maintain charity settings only within their authorized mainstream-model scope, including eligible unbound mainstream candidates. Shared key settings can affect every model using that key. Managers do not receive configured key secrets; original provider-error diagnostics have the separate exception described above. New donations require a yes/no choice about manual Discord public thanks; submission makes that choice immutable. Old unconfirmed records are not permission for public thanks. Review records preserve the acting role and remove its account link on deletion. Public model settings are shared configuration, not a creator’s private export. Authorized discovery can refresh managed donation keys without showing their secrets. Failure thresholds default to 10; zero disables error-triggered removal only. Counts and ordinary expiry, withdrawal, manual switches and quotas retain their effect. The safe current threshold and owned-key limits are included in account export. Forced rejection of an automatically approved donation stops new charity calls while preserving personal use and settled rewards. To recognize the same key when submitted again, the service retains non-reversible matching material, review requirements and necessary review records without automatic expiry. A different account, address, connector or account deletion does not remove the review requirement. Only keys enabled in that manual approval are cleared. Matching material is internal and excluded from API responses and personal exports. Managed manual model candidates belong to the donated resource and still need separate verification and binding; the donor’s personal catalog stays unchanged.
privacy.keyLimitsBody: The concurrency and RPM limits you set for a service key apply to both personal and charity model calls. Your account export includes these settings. Administrators and level-6 stewards can read them on resources they are authorized to manage, but cannot change them. The settings are deleted with the key.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This policy describes the data used to operate a NonbiriAPI instance.
privacy.notice: Deployment template: before accepting real users, the instance operator must replace the operator identity, contact channel, effective date, retention details and governing-law statements as required by the deployment and applicable law. This text is not legal advice.
privacy.operatorBody: NonbiriAPI is open-source software. Each deployed instance is operated independently by the person or organization that controls it. This policy applies to data processed by that operator, not to the public source repository or to Discord and third-party AI services acting under their own policies.
privacy.identityBody: The user station uses Discord for registration and sign-in. The service receives a Discord identifier, username, avatar information, and the membership information needed to check server and role eligibility. Sign-in tokens are used only during sign-in and are not stored as account data. The service keeps limited account, sign-in, and preference information and protects sign-in cookies according to the deployment configuration.
privacy.dataBody: The service stores your account profile, preferences, endpoints, encrypted service keys, discovered models, platform models, donations, usage, check-ins, activities and games. Some resource settings describe how to forward a request; they do not contain the request itself. The service stores up to 10 private battle Custom presets on your account, with the mode, character, optional Harness and ordered skills, to fill pre-match choices. They stay with your account beyond 30-day match-history cleanup, appear in your own export, and are removed when you delete your account. Loading a preset never queues or charges you. An account API key is shown in full once, after which only verification and identification material remains. Account export contains your safe resources, four asset balances and financial history, game records and available randomness proofs, donation limits, activity exchanges, safe image-task outcomes and inactivity actions. It excludes full keys, encrypted key content, sign-in tokens, raw diagnostics, source IP and client clues, risk evidence, private administrator configuration, prompts, images, full execution parameters, internal upstream task identifiers, unrevealed game secrets and other users’ identities. The service also stores model message-role settings, private preset names and Lake Notes profiles. Batch imports and connection updates retain targets and per-item results for up to 24 hours so you can check interrupted work. Imported keys remain encrypted under the credential policy; operation records keep no additional plaintext key or note. Your export includes personal model settings, preset names and unexpired results, excluding private retry, matching and unrevealed reward material.
privacy.creditHistoryBody: You can filter your own credit history by asset. A mixed payment or activity exchange can appear as separate asset entries for the same operation. Entries related to your API calls can link to your request logs while those logs remain available. Donation rewards do not reveal another user's request ID or logs. Request-log expiry does not remove credit history.
privacy.economyBody: The service records separate general-credit and game-credit wallets, each of which may be negative. General check-ins, donation rewards and game winnings go to general credits. Game check-ins and daily welfare go to game credits. API calls, Thursday contributions and Thursday rewards use General Credits; insufficient General Credits do not cause a Game Credit debit. Game admission uses available game credits first and general credits for the remainder. Eligible refunds return the original assets; remaining stakes at a normal Rock Paper Scissors finish and game winnings use general credits. Each change records its asset and amount. The cumulative donor-reward total is a lifetime statistic used for donation summaries and level requirements, not spendable funds. No game result or economic return is guaranteed, and level 4 provides no game-economy advantage. Leaderboards are anonymous by default. Choosing a public profile shows your current server nickname or username and Discord avatar URL; no avatar copy or historical profile copy is stored. Draft paper and brushes are separate whole-unit activity assets; they are not game-payment funds and cannot be exchanged back to general/game credits or into each other.
privacy.credentialsBody: Configured service keys are not deliberately exposed through ordinary lists, alerts, caller errors, exports or URLs. An upstream may echo a credential into the restricted original-error diagnostics described below. The browser receives only the information needed to describe a key and does not save the full service key or account API key. Deleting a key or account immediately stops future calls through it. Encrypted key content that no longer belongs to any resource is cleared within one hour. An OpenAI-compatible key can ask the connected service not to store requests (store=false), but that service may ignore or reject the request. This is not a promise of zero retention and does not control the provider's abuse monitoring. Operators must still protect the server, complete backups, and master-key file.
privacy.trafficBody: Forwarded requests create limited records such as the account, model, service used, time, status, duration, and available token usage. Request bodies and successful response bodies are not actively logged; restricted original upstream errors follow the separate policy below. Debug starts in preview mode: it does not access a key, send a request outside the site, set aside charity credits, or record usage. Each real send requires separate confirmation and may use provider quota or charity credits. Debug request and response summaries with sensitive content removed exist only in the current process and page memory. They are not written to the database, ordinary logs, alerts, exports, backups, URLs, or browser storage, and are cleared when the session closes, is replaced, or expires, and on sign-out, restriction, account deletion, or service restart. Disconnecting the Debug page does not cancel an original request made with an account API key. Administrators and current level-6 stewards can read and export the same limited request logs, including the caller’s site ID and actual charges. Details also show routing key identifiers for each attempt. Their charity logs also show the caller’s latest synced Discord name and ID. Deleted identity data is not restored. An active legal preservation requirement may allow these managers to read an older record by its ID; it does not extend ordinary lists or exports. Steward reads of these held records retain first and last access times and a count with the preservation record. Account deletion removes the steward identity from that audit. Chat and embedding inputs, including text and Token IDs, are processed for the requested operation. Returned vectors are used for the response only and are not saved in Debug or persistent records. Authenticated requests refused before the model handler may also record the safe refusal stage and reason, without an upstream attempt, Token usage or model-call fee. A separately configured abuse deduction remains a distinct financial operation. An endpoint owner or charity administrator can configure bounded forwarded and fixed headers, and body defaults or forced fields for future requests. The upstream can receive them. Secret values are redacted in configuration reads and excluded from ordinary export. After self-deletion, administrator deletion or inactivity removal, request logs, necessary source details and original account/Discord associations remain for 30 days after completion, or for an applicable legal hold. Only authorized administrators and level-6 stewards can read them. Missing historical identity stays unknown. A new account using the same Discord identity cannot read or export old logs. After denied sign-in, the verified person can read current reasons for five minutes using a separate explanation-only credential. Operator identity is omitted.
privacy.sharingBody: Request content may be sent to OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible or native AI SDK Gateway v3 services selected by the account owner, including donor-provided charity resources operated by OpenAI, Anthropic, or another independent third party. A third party may process or retain request content, account logs, or abuse-monitoring data under its own policy, which the instance operator cannot control. A charity donor controls the related third-party account or key and may therefore see full request content in that service's account logs. Donating a key alone does not give access to caller identity or request content in this site's interface; authorized steward access is described separately. OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible requests also include a system-generated safety code that can be linked only for the same user, deployment, and third-party service. It hides direct identity but is not fully anonymous. Discord processes sign-in activity under its own policy. The operator may disclose data when required by law or needed to protect the service, users, or public safety, and must describe access by other data processors, hosting providers, and support staff. For OpenAI-compatible embeddings, this code replaces the request's user field; caller-supplied identity in that field is not forwarded. Native AI SDK Gateway v3 calls omit cost attribution by default. If the administrator enables it, chat and text embedding calls send a server-generated pseudonym scoped to the user and final gateway origin. The gateway can link requests in that scope for cost attribution. The label is not anonymous, contains no raw account or Discord ID, and does not mean that the gateway applies a safety identifier. Callers cannot override it. Debug shows only whether the label was sent, not its value.
privacy.retentionBody: Request logs and necessary sources remain until 30 days after completion or an applicable hold, including after self, administrator or inactivity deletion. Recurring donation limits store rule settings, usage and in-flight reservations. Completed sliding-window usage totals are kept for at most 35 days; fixed periods keep the current period and any older period still needed to finish a call. Unfinished accounting keeps only the facts needed to settle it. These totals contain no request content or caller identity. Shared donation handling follows the donation's retention period; deleting its processing actor removes the account link without keeping a name or Discord copy. Records of completed donations and reviews, daily activity summaries, and completed charity payment holds are kept for 400 days. After a donated key ends or its service key is deleted, non-reversible information used only to match new abuse reports may remain for up to 90 days and cannot be used to make a call. The minimum target and donation-source relationship already saved for a report follows that case's own 90-day period or an active legal preservation requirement. Viewing a record does not extend these periods, and legal preservation does not extend the new-report matching period. Fishing, LinkLink and Rock Paper Scissors rounds, settlements, and shared results are kept for 30 days after settlement; a paid but unfinished round remains until settlement, and a private Rock Paper Scissors result remains until you acknowledge it or delete the account. LinkLink boards show each user's best completed score by size over 7 or 30 days, with earlier achievements first for equal scores. Fishing personal bests, asset-tagged credit changes, profile-visibility preferences, and the completion time and award for each once-only game newcomer task remain for the life of the account. Newcomer completion records are included in your export and deleted with your account. Administrators and current level-6 stewards can read non-administrator account profiles, limits, levels, both wallets and usage. Stewards may modify only other current level-1–5 accounts and cannot delete accounts or change cumulative donor credit; they can also manage announcements and donated-key failure streaks. These actions retain audits without secrets. Announcement audits last 365 days with actor identity removed after 90 days; donation reviews follow the 400-day donation retention. Debug content is not stored long term. Sign-in sessions expire after inactivity or their maximum lifetime. Resolved administrator alerts are cleared after 30 days; unresolved alerts are subject to number limits and duplicate merging. Export allows up to 10,000 rows in each collection and 16 MiB for the complete JSON. An oversized export fails clearly and is not shortened. Account deletion invalidates sign-in sessions and account API keys, clears private account projections, while retained logs and minimum management safety records follow the restricted access and deadlines described here. Late callbacks cannot recreate the account. Complete operator backups and third-party services may retain copies under their own policies. Bidding Duel and Turn-based Battle Minigame (Test) keep participant-accessible full match records for 30 days after settlement. After that, complete rule traces remain in an administrator-only anonymous archive without user references, original match or operation IDs, absolute times, payment sources or cross-match identity links. During a match, unused opposing equipment stays hidden; personal exports omit opposing identities and saved profile copies. Administrator batch export uses bounded pages and expiring signed continuation cursors. Blackjack's corresponding retention is described below. Blackjack stores waiting entries, the original funding of each stake, hands and actions, frozen terms, preset emotes and settlement facts. Participants and spectators can see the names and avatars of players currently seated, together with revealed cards, stakes, results and emotes. Other players' wallet balances and funding sources remain private. Live names and avatars are not copied into retained table records or personal export. Dealer hole cards and the undealt sequence are not provided to players during decisions. Participants and administrators can read game records for 30 days after settlement, followed by administrator-only anonymous long-term facts without account references, original game IDs, absolute times, funding sources or emotes. Waiting entries persist across rounds without a waiting timeout until seating, voluntary departure or removal under maintenance, game closure, ban or account-deletion rules. Account export includes safe personal queue and game records within the 10,000-row per-game and 16 MiB total bounds. Deletion detaches identity and auto-stands its hands without cancelling other players. The six games also store an independent random seed, opening commitment and bounded draw transcript for each game. Unrevealed seeds, future draws and hidden plans stay on the server and are not provided to players through state, logs or account exports. Before a multi-stage game ends, its proof provides only public information such as the commitment. Blackjack reveals its seed after the whole table finishes decisions and the result commits; Bidding Duel, Turn-based Battle Minigame (Test), Three-player Rock Paper Scissors and LinkLink reveal after the entire game ends. The presentation in each battle round does not end the match. Instantly settled Fishing batches provide proofs alongside results; cancelled games may reveal after the server commits cancellation. Participants can verify and download proofs, including safe proofs in account export. Current Blackjack table spectators can read that table's public proof but do not gain participant history access. Proofs follow their parent records, with personal access lasting at most 30 days after completion; anonymous archives remove seeds, commitments and proofs. The Site cannot subsequently remove public material already downloaded or saved by others. Loan records retain the accepted terms, time, linked financial operation and actual balances until account deletion. Temporary newcomer qualifications are released when their game resolves or is cancelled; safe qualification metadata is included in the personal export. Game rankings keep net-spending contributions for seven days, positive Bidding and Blackjack profit contributions for 30 days, and necessary historical totals until deletion. Ranking preferences and cumulative charity achievement times follow the account. Charity visibility is separate from game visibility and defaults to anonymous; banned accounts stay on leaderboards anonymously without their avatar. Active automatic penalties remain available, ended penalties and direct deductions for 90 days; ordinary request links disappear after 30 days. Current violation windows survive service restarts and are trimmed to the configured window. After deletion, minimum unexpired facts can remain to prevent bypass through re-registration with the same Discord identity. Personal exports contain safe penalty summaries and adjustments, not internal thresholds, counted events or management evidence. Administrators and current level-6 stewards can read the authorized penalty history, rule snapshots and bounded evidence; historical restrictions without that evidence are identified as such. When you delete your account, a separate minimum read-only security record keeps only known former site and Discord IDs, registration and deletion times, effective level, restriction state, deletion source and balances before zeroing. Missing historical fields remain unknown. Administrators and current level-6 stewards can view authorized records; only administrators can see deletion-alert links and minimal records of active duels actually aborted by self-deletion. Those duel-abort records are cleared after 90 days; the minimum deleted-account record has no automatic expiry. A separate administrator-only economic deletion alert retains the balance snapshot; a negative general or game balance leaves it unresolved unless automatic blacklisting succeeds, which resolves it in the same transaction; other deletion alerts start resolved. A Discord blacklist entry and its first reason remain until administrator removal; later reasons are appended. Self-deletion under an effective ban, charity pause or negative general/game balance can add an event. Limited already-used reward eligibility and unexpired violation windows can continue for a new account with the same Discord identity, without restoring the old account or its other private data. These management security records are excluded from personal exports. Model-role settings follow their resource lifecycle. Batch-operation results expire after 24 hours; retries do not extend that period. Account deletion clears these records. Key-review matching information and necessary review records have no automatic expiry and remain subject to the management access described above.
privacy.rightsBody: Subject to applicable law and the instance operator's process, you can update supported account settings, request an export and delete your account through the elevated self-service flow. Deletion is destructive. Contact the instance operator for access, correction, restriction or other privacy requests; the operator must publish the appropriate contact channel before production use.
privacy.securityBody: The service checks resource ownership, encrypts stored keys, prevents requests from reaching protected network locations or following dangerous redirects, limits resource use, and stops later work when a request is cancelled. Sensitive responses ask browsers and intermediate services not to cache them. The OpenAI-only “convert tool calls to text” experiment converts only complete real calls and results. It never runs tools or invents results and may affect normal tool workflows; Anthropic connections cannot use it. No system is completely secure. Do not place keys in notes, model names, URLs, tool data, issue reports, or support messages.
privacy.contactBody: The instance operator must publish a privacy contact, effective date and applicable jurisdiction in this page before production use. Material changes to data collection, sharing or retention should be announced and handled according to applicable law.
privacy.diagnosticsBody: We do not actively record request bodies or successful response bodies. For troubleshooting, we retain original upstream failures from personal and charity calls, retries, streaming error events, model discovery and image-activity operations. An upstream error can echo your input, prompt or a credential; that original content may be retained. Only current administrators and level-6 stewards may read it, even when a request belongs to another user. Ordinary retention is 30 days, with at most 1 MiB per error and an administrator-configurable total payload budget of 1 GiB by default. Truncation, unavailable bodies and capacity omissions are identified. At capacity, new bodies are omitted while safe summaries remain. An explicit legal preservation requirement can extend the approved records’ retention, and those bodies still count toward the budget. Ordinary caller errors remain sanitized.
privacy.sourcesBody: We also retain the effective source IP, its trust quality and a limited set of client clues: User-Agent, the originating site from Origin/Referer/HTTP-Referer, client titles and selected SDK language, version and runtime headers. URL paths, query strings and fragments are not retained in these origin fields. This information is bounded, normally retained for 30 days and visible only to administrators and level-6 stewards. It is not included in personal exports. Client headers are self-reported and can be absent, forged or changed by a relay; a shared IP can represent a household or shared network.
privacy.scanBody: Manual client and address audits retain the initiator, selected filters and rules, progress and related request references for up to 24 hours, with at most 100,000 results per scan. Only the initiating administrator or level-6 steward with current permission can read the task; deleting that account invalidates it. Deletion of an audited account preserves log references still within their original retention period or legal hold. When source records are cleared, affected results are removed or marked as changed. Audits neither collect request bodies nor enter personal exports. Image-model discovery diagnostics record the actual GET address and empty request body under the existing diagnostic access and retention rules.
privacy.auditBody: Administrators and level-6 stewards may review sustained RPM or concurrency use, shared source addresses and manually maintained client clues for both personal and charity calls. Initial defaults flag at least 80% of the effective quota for five complete consecutive minutes, or at least three distinct Discord identities using the same trusted API address within 24 hours. Review pages identify coverage gaps and supporting observations; a match does not prove misuse and these new findings do not automatically punish an account. Existing configured abuse rules continue independently. Selected model-list and compatibility-probe requests also contribute bounded access events: only valid account API keys link an event to an account and key generation, while unauthenticated requests contribute separate anonymous counts without an IP or client identity record. Key rotation, revocation and deletion remove key attribution. Administrators alone can inspect separate issuance, retirement, transfers and stock for each of the four assets; refunds and internal transfers are not treated as new issuance. Manual review can also group one Discord identity across old/current accounts when it uses at least three trusted API addresses in rolling 24 hours; administrators can adjust the window and threshold. Shared-address counts deduplicate Discord identities. Website sign-ins, unreliable fallback proxy addresses and request bodies are excluded, and findings do not automatically punish users.
privacy.imageBody: Draft paper and brushes are separate whole-unit activity balances. Exchanges, reservations, charges and refunds have their own ledger records. The execution copy of image prompts and complete parameters stays only in server memory and is not actively written to request logs or the database. The configured independent provider receives them to generate the image. Valid image results stay only in server memory for a ten-minute pickup window and in the browser memory after loading; the service does not save images to disk, the database or successful-response logs. Closing the page, expiry or a service restart can lose a result. A successful task is not refunded for that loss. Safe task status, image counts and charging outcomes remain available for 30 days; financial records follow the ledger policy and safe facts are included in your export. Queue views show totals and your own position, not the identities of other participants. Raw provider failures follow the restricted diagnostic policy above. A price preview reads current model rules without requesting generation. The selected size and accepted model and price revisions fix a task's charge; later configuration edits do not reprice it.

terms.fatFishBody: Fat Fish uses General credits only. Any unlock price, ticket price and rewards are shown before you confirm. Unlocking and starting are separate charges; preparation alone does not charge a ticket. A started game keeps its original deadline through backgrounding, refresh or a connection loss. Results and rewards depend on server verification, not the displayed local score. Voluntary abandonment, self-deletion, invalid inputs and late submissions do not refund a started ticket. Confirmed platform verification faults, administrator cancellation, bans and administrator or system account deletion refund an unsettled ticket to its original source; past unlock charges are not refunded. One-time rewards cannot be claimed again by deleting and re-registering the same identity. Closing or pausing admission does not grant extra play time to a game already accepted.
terms.title: Terms of service
terms.intro: By using a NonbiriAPI instance, you agree to use it lawfully and protect your own credentials.
terms.notice: Deployment template: the instance operator must replace the operator identity, contact channel, effective date, governing law and complaint process before accepting real users. This text is not legal advice.
terms.operatorBody: NonbiriAPI is open-source gateway software, not an AI model provider. The operator of a particular instance controls its access rules, connected third-party services, limits, maintenance, and user support. The public source project and its copyright holder do not automatically operate every deployment.
terms.accessBody: An account may require Discord OAuth and membership of a configured server and role. You are responsible for activity performed through your account and must provide information that is accurate enough for the operator's access and support process. The operator may pause new registration or suspend access for security, maintenance, legal compliance or a breach of these terms.
terms.useBody: Use only endpoints, credentials and models that you are authorized to access. Do not use the service for unlawful activity, fraud, abuse, unauthorized access, credential theft, malware, harassment, privacy violations, sexual exploitation of minors, non-consensual intimate imagery, attacks against providers or other users, denial of service, rate-limit bypassing or attempts to defeat ownership and security controls.
terms.upstreamBody: Requests may be processed by OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible or native AI SDK Gateway v3 services selected by the account owner, including donor-provided charity resources. You must follow each service provider's terms, usage policies, licensing conditions, and content restrictions. A provider may keep request content, account logs, or abuse-monitoring data under its own policy. A request not to store content (store:false) may be ignored or rejected and is not a promise of zero retention. The operator does not guarantee that a third party will accept a request, preserve content, or keep an account available. Embedding calls require a compatible provider and model. Site chat-only request-storage and tool-conversion settings do not change embedding requests. A successful charity batch counts as one call; Token pricing uses all reported input tokens, and missing usage follows the displayed reserve rules. Native AI SDK Gateway v3 calls omit cost attribution by default. If the administrator enables it, chat and text embedding calls send a server-generated pseudonym scoped to the user and final gateway origin. The gateway can link requests in that scope for cost attribution. The label is not anonymous, contains no raw account or Discord ID, and does not mean that the gateway applies a safety identifier. Callers cannot override it. Debug shows only whether the label was sent, not its value. Each model can use its protocol’s usual handling for extra message roles or preserve, convert or reject selected roles. Conversion may change how the provider interprets a message. The default keeps the protocol’s usual behavior; tool-associated messages follow the separate tool settings.
terms.credentialsBody: Keep service keys, account API keys, sign-in links, and recovery information confidential. Replace a key immediately if it may have been exposed. Do not put keys in notes, URLs, model names, tools, issue reports, or support messages. You are responsible for submitted content and must have the right to send it to the selected provider. The experimental “convert tool calls to text” feature changes only how calls are displayed and sent. It does not run a tool, create a result, or prove success, and it may affect programs that expect structured tool calls. You may use your site API key to import authorized provider keys into an existing personal service or append connections to an existing personal model. Items are saved separately; completed items remain after a failure, disconnection or cancellation. Duplicate keys retain their existing record and settings, and duplicate connections keep their order. Manual mode saves configuration; availability requires separate verification. After interruption, check with the original request and operation identifier within 24 hours. After that window, inspect the actual resources first. Revoking or rotating a key stops further operations with the old key.
terms.availabilityBody: Requests may be rate-limited, rejected, retried, or temporarily unavailable because of quotas, resource ownership, safety checks, third-party failures, maintenance, or permissions. A complete response is required for success; an HTTP status alone does not guarantee the result. Debug preview sends nothing outside the site, while a separately confirmed real send may consume provider quota or charity credits. Game prices, random results, recovery, and settlement are handled consistently by the game system and offer no guaranteed result or return. The operator may change limits or discontinue a prerelease service. Bidding Duel and Turn-based Battle Minigame (Test) freeze their displayed entry price and fees when you queue. Game credits are spent first, then general credits. Queue cancellation, unmatched expiry, draws and system cancellations refund the original payment split. A decided match refunds the winner's entry and pays the loser's net entry as general credits after separately rounded fees. Surrender is a loss; disconnecting does not pause deadlines. A server restart, ban or deletion cancels an unfinished match. The battle presentation does not delay final accounting. Game points and resources do not have cash value. Blackjack starts at each server :00 and :30: 5 seconds for seating, 20 for simultaneous decisions and 5 for results. An early table finish may start results sooner, but the next game keeps its scheduled start. There is one table with up to nine seats; others may spectate. Up to 4,096 waiting players keep their first accepted FIFO position across rounds, unchanged by duplicate requests or refreshes. Waiters may leave at any time; seated players may leave before the 5-second deadline and be replaced in order. No replacements occur after that deadline. Once the whole game settles, participants must explicitly rejoin the tail, without reserved seats or automatic replay. Queue entry freezes terms and reserves the base stake using Game Credits first, then General Credits; changing the amount requires leaving and rejoining. Splits and doubles reserve additional stakes; insufficient funds reject the addition without changing the hand. Each hand's gross return pays separate platform, welfare and Thursday fees, defaulting to 1% each. All net returns, including pushes and principal, are General Credits; zero returns incur no extra fee. Under the defaults, a stake of 1,000 returns 0 for a loss, 970 for a push, 1,940 for an ordinary win and 2,425 for a natural blackjack. The game page shows full table rules, stake limits and fees. Long-term expected returns are negative, no individual outcome is guaranteed, and card order is not adjusted to a player's wins or losses. Waiting departures, exits within the seating window and system cancellations refund the actual original funding without fees. After dealing, disconnection, closing the page or timeout continues play with automatic standing and does not itself trigger a refund. Restart cancels the unsettled table while preserving unseated waiters and their reservations; committed results are never reversed. Maintenance or game closure refunds waiters and undealt seats while dealt tables finish. Banned dealt hands stand automatically. Deletion detaches identity while play finishes; unavailable proceeds go to the corresponding external asset account without recreating the account. The six games use independent cryptographically secure random seeds. You can save an opening commitment and verify or download the disclosed seed and draws after the server commits completion or cancellation of the whole game. Blackjack reveals during results after all table decisions end; Likes keeps its seed secret during intermediate round presentations. Instantly completed Fishing batches provide proofs only alongside results. Verification reproduces recorded draws and checks the seed against the original commitment; older games without proofs cannot be retroactively verified. Commitments do not guarantee returns and alone cannot prove the operator never preselected a seed. Game pages describe rules, public actions and verification. Each donated key has a consecutive-failure disable threshold, default 10, editable by its donor, an administrator or a current steward, including permitted steward automation. Saving retains the count and immediately recalculates error-disablement. Zero never disables for errors, although errors are still counted and success clears the count. Pages warn persistently without an extra confirmation. Manual disabling, expiry, withdrawal, bans and quotas still apply. The current threshold is included in safe account exports; policy audit records contain no key secrets and follow donation-review retention. When the optional loan activity is enabled, confirmation immediately adds the displayed game credits and deducts the displayed repayment from general credits, including the disclosed fee and interest. These are site credits, not a cash loan. A nonnegative general balance is required before borrowing, but repayment can make it negative; later general-credit income reduces that negative balance. Game credits remain usable. Each quote expires after 60 seconds or a configuration change and must be refreshed and confirmed again. The accepted record shows actual balances; displayed estimates can change before confirmation. Loan activity does not earn donor credit or count toward game rankings. Newcomer tasks pay once per account after eligible normal play, may stack in one result, and do not award for local teaching or system cancellation. Game leaderboards follow the stated net-spending or positive-profit calculation and exclude loans and newcomer awards. Optional sound and reduced-motion settings change presentation only; results and financial settlement remain server-controlled. New donation submissions and pending edits require a meaningful nonblank description.
terms.dataBody: The privacy policy describes information stored by the service, Debug handling, exports, and account deletion. After identity verification, deleting an account removes linked donation, charity, check-in, credit-change, and game data. The service opens only a structurally complete database that passes validation; an unrecognized, damaged, or incompatible database is rejected. A separately confirmed clean deployment first creates and verifies a complete snapshot, then removes the current database—including accounts, business data, site settings, and custom legal text—and starts with an empty database. A protected operator backup may retain the database, program, environment, and master key for recovery. The new environment must remain in maintenance with registration, activities, charity access, donation intake, and games closed until legal text, required settings, and initial data have been reapplied and checked. Backup recovery and third-party data retention follow the operator's and provider's respective policies. Bidding Duel, Turn-based Battle Minigame (Test) and Blackjack remove participant identity links; de-identified rule traces may remain long term as described in the Privacy Policy. Dealt Blackjack games continue automatic settlement without restoring the deleted account. Random proofs follow the Privacy Policy's cleanup periods and do not enter anonymous long-term archives. terms.donationBody: A new donation requires an explicit choice about allowing an administrator or level-6 steward to thank you manually in a Discord public channel. You cannot change that choice after submission; older unconfirmed records do not authorize public thanks. Charity calls cannot use your own donated keys unless you are currently a level-6 steward; personal models remain available under their normal rules. Exempt calls retain ordinary donor rewards. Donation limits may independently restrict total, input and output Tokens, and shared key changes affect all bindings. Charity-model forwarding can remove the configured optional top-level parameters. A recent success percentage describes the displayed observation window and sample, not a promise that your next request will succeed. Forced rejection stops new charity calls; dispatched calls settle under the existing rules, and personal use and settled rewards remain. Resubmitting the same key may require manual review and explicit enablement. Failure streaks count provider errors, connection failures and timeouts. User cancellation, downstream disconnection and platform rejection leave the streak unchanged; a provider error confirmed before cancellation still counts. Counting and charges are separate, and cancellation may still incur a charge. Charity automation reads and writes require level 6; level 5 retains personal automation and its existing browser permissions.
terms.imageBody: Limited activities need a configured opening period. Hiding an activity removes its directory entry but does not block an otherwise eligible visitor with its link. Reopening keeps balances and history. The picture-book activity exchanges general credits for draft paper and brushes; it does not support reverse exchange or exchange between those currencies. The default prices are 1,000 general credits per draft paper and 10,000 per brush. Brush supply is a cumulative shared cap, initially ten; reducing the cap does not confiscate existing balances, and task refunds do not restore exchange supply. Administrators may change future prices and settings. A no-charge quote lets you review the selected size and exact price without requesting an image. Submitting reserves both quoted currency amounts multiplied by the requested image count under the accepted model and pricing revisions. If a revision changes first, review a fresh quote. Any valid partial success charges the full accepted task price. Failure, an unresolved result at the execution deadline, or cancellation before dispatch refunds both currencies. After dispatch you cannot cancel, and closing the page does not cancel. The server controls ordering and upstream requests; no participant receives a privileged queue or free allowance. Default queue and execution limits are 30 minutes each. Successful images have a ten-minute memory pickup window and may be lost on page closure, expiry or restart without a refund. Restart refunds queued tasks whose in-memory payload was lost; an uncertain upstream submission is never automatically repeated. Natural activity end lets accepted work finish, while manual pause or maintenance cancels undispatched tasks and refunds them. Bans prevent result access; account deletion removes private data while minimal anonymous execution cleanup may continue. Administrators open Lake Notes for defined periods. The entry fee is shown before confirmation and charged at most once per period in general credits. Device changes, price edits and reopening after a pause do not repeat that fee; another period may charge separately. Profiles and coins persist across periods. Ending, pause or maintenance preserves progress and stops play and exchanges. The four directions between coins and general or game credits are configured separately and start disabled. Exchanges use the confirmed whole-lot quantity and preserve the remainder; a price change requires fresh confirmation. These virtual assets have no cash redemption, withdrawal or user-to-user transfer. Custom picture-book dimensions must have an applicable quote; price changes require reselection and confirmation.
terms.inactivityBody: An administrator may enable an inactivity policy; it is disabled by default. The user site displays the applicable rules and expected processing dates. Successful login or API use, check-ins, benefit claims and effective game/activity actions count as activity; passive rewards and background polling do not. Administrators and levels 5 and 6 are exempt, but owning a usable donated key does not create an exemption. Configured decay affects only positive available general/game balances, with separate rates or fixed amounts, periods and retained floors. It does not take frozen funds or activity currencies or deepen a negative balance. First enablement, re-enablement and stricter rules grant at least seven days. A missed series of decay periods is caught up at most once; if protective banning is due at the same check, banning takes priority without decay. A protective permanent ban preserves the account and balances, stops future decay, and can be reversed by an administrator, restarting observation. Existing donations remain usable and earn normal rewards only for this protective ban reason; the banned account still cannot log in or call APIs.

personalAutomation.title: Manage your resources with scripts
personalAutomation.intro: Use scripts to import keys into existing services or append connections to existing models, as needed.
personalAutomation.identityTitle: Prepare your API key and targets
personalAutomation.identity: Authenticate with the account API key (CallerKey) generated on this page, using Bearer authentication. Replace the sample placeholders locally.
personalAutomation.scope: Personal routes manage only your own resources, including for level 5 and 6 stewards. All community automation reads and writes require a current level 6 steward.
personalAutomation.lookup: Query services, keys and models first and use their returned IDs. These routes do not create services or platform models and never return key plaintext.
personalAutomation.key: Read settings for one service key
personalAutomation.pagination: Lists accept q, page and page_size: page 1 and 20 items by default, with 10/20/50/100 items allowed. Single-object reads have no query parameters. GET needs no body or Idempotency-Key.
personalAutomation.import: Import keys you are authorized to use into an existing service with ownership_confirmed:true. An identical key already in that service returns its original ID and preserves its note, enabled state and settings. Import does not discover or call models.
personalAutomation.bind: One request selects an existing model, one upstream model name and several of your keys. An identical existing connection returns its original ID without overwriting, reordering or enabling disabled resources.
personalAutomation.catalog: catalog_mode defaults to manual: it adds a missing manual catalog entry without claiming upstream verification. refresh requires successful discovery containing the requested upstream name; failure or an empty catalog never falls back to manual.
personalAutomation.result: Inspect results even after HTTP 200: success is confirmed, failed is a confirmed failure, and incomplete is unconfirmed. Other failures do not undo successful items. existing confirms the resource exists, not that it is currently callable.
personalAutomation.retry: A lost response or cancellation does not prove rollback. Within 24 hours, use the original Idempotency-Key and complete original body to check and continue unfinished items; do not switch keys and repeat. Correct confirmed failures and start a new operation only for that failed subset. After 24 hours, query resources first.
personalAutomation.limits: Each batch accepts 1–100 items and a total body of up to 256 KiB. Import has 30 seconds; binding has 60 seconds, with up to 15 seconds per discovery. Requests at the concurrency limit return 429 immediately. Cancellation stops further processing.
personalAutomation.statuses: At least one success returns 200; all confirmed failures return 422; no success with unfinished items returns 504. Reusing the same key with different content returns 409.
